data.gender_notes: Muammar is used as a male name in Islamic naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Muammar is a name derived from the Arabic root 'm-r-m', which means 'commander of an army'. In Islamic history, Muammar bin Abdul Wadud is known as the legendary Berber general who defended against the invading Byzantine and Roman forces. This name is a reminder of strength and resilience in the face of adversity. The name Muammar carries the meaning “Commander of an army” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in Arabic, Urdu, Persian. Parents who choose Muammar usually hope their child will grow to embody commander of an army and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of courage and determination in the service of Islam.
data.etymology: Muammar belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “Commander of an army.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Muammar total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_urdu.name: معمّر

data.cultural_impact: The name Muammar holds significant cultural importance in the Islamic world, as it is associated with one of the most formidable military leaders in early Islamic history. Muammar ibn Abdul Wadud was a Berber general who effectively defended Africa against invasions by the Byzantine and Roman Empires. The name is a symbol of courage, resilience, and military prowess. Muammar's legendary accomplishments continue to inspire and have an impact on the Islamic community, particularly in North Africa, where his name remains a source of pride and celebration.
